# The scorecard

The cells at the top of a goal’s page: against plan, since last week, what’s left, and how likely it is to hit the target.

## The rule

`goalScorecard(goal, cycle, checkIns, week, stale)` gives a few cells, each a key, a label, a value, a muted line under it (*sub*) and a tone (`good`, `bad` or `flat`). *stale* is true when the official status is `stale`: then nothing is projected. Every number comes from the rules above; the scorecard only words them, and decides one thing of its own: the likelihood.

**How likely** (`likelihood(mark, projection, better, floor)`), worked in the better direction (+1 when higher is better): *half* = max(half the projected range's width, *floor*, 10⁻⁹); *d* = (*mark* − likeliest value) × *better* / *half*. *d* ≤ −0.5: **Likely**; ≤ 1: **Possible**; ≤ 2: **Unlikely**; above: **Very unlikely**. Words, never a percentage. The floor for a target is max(2% of the planned change, half the goal's last decimal place); for a limit, the same with the margin (or 10% of the limit when there is no margin) in place of the planned change.

**A number to move** (judged as in [the status](status.md), from what has been posted):

| Cell | Value |
|---|---|
| `plan`, Vs plan | the latest number against the plan for its own week, rounded to the goal's decimals and said in the better direction: "9 hours behind plan", "3 pts ahead of plan", "On plan". No number: "No value yet". Sub: "plan 43.85%", plus "in week 4" when the latest check-in is older than this week |
| `since`, Vs last week (Last change when stale) | the change from the check-in before with a number: "4 pts better" or "worse", "No change", or "First check-in". Sub: "was 40% in week 3" |
| `target`, To target | what's left, "12 pts to go", or Target reached. When lower is better the amount is over the target and says so: "5 min over". Sub: "target 75%", plus "by week 40" when due before the cycle's end |
| `hit`, Will it hit 75%? | the likelihood of reaching the target by its due week; "Can’t say" when stale; "Too early to say" with no projection. Sub: "likely 52% by cycle end" |

**Tones.** `plan`: ahead `good`, behind `bad`, on plan or no number `flat`. `since`: better `good`, worse `bad`, otherwise `flat` (the check-in before is the latest earlier one, by week then posting, that has a number). `target`: reached `good`, else `flat`. `hit`: Likely `good`, Possible `flat`, Unlikely and Very unlikely `bad`, Can’t say and Too early `flat`. `limit`: outside `bad`, near `flat`, inside `good`. `room`: over `bad`, within the margin (room ≤ margin) `flat`, else `good`. `done`: at least as many done as are due `good`, else `flat`. `late`: any behind `bad`, none `good`. `next`: expected after its due week `bad`, else `flat`; All done `good`. The likelihood floor uses the goal's current plan; a margin of 0 counts as none.

**A number to keep in range:** `limit` (Inside it, Inside, near it, Outside it), `since`, `room` (how far inside or over the limit) and `hit` (Will it stay within?, or Back within by the end? when outside; the likelihood of ending on the safe side of the limit at the cycle's end).

**Dated stages:** `done` (stages done of all, with how many are due by this week), `late` (stages behind their dates, slipping or late, and by up to how many weeks) and `next` (the week the next stage now lands, or All done).

A stopped goal has no `hit` cell.

**Short or over** (`shortWord(better)` in `src/domain/vocabulary.ts`, the one place the word is chosen): an amount on the wrong side of a plan or target is "short" when higher is better and "over" when lower is better: "1 pt short" of a 46% plan, "1 min over" a 6 min plan. The scorecard's `target` cell, the chart's mark at the due week ("5 over") and a quarter's result ("Q3: 7 min against a plan of 6 min, 1 min over") all use it.

**A quarter's result** (`quarterResult` in `src/domain/year.ts`) compares the number with the plan at the quarter's end as both are shown, at the goal's decimals: 0.68 against a plan shown as 0.68 is met, never "0.00 short".

## Worked examples

Each is run against the real rule by `src/spec/spec.test.ts`: the result is what the code gives.

| Given | The rule gives |
|---|---|
| A target of 75, higher is better, projected 80 (range 78–82, d = −2.5); 76 (72–80, d = −0.25); 72 (70–74, d = 1.5); 60 (58–62, d = 7.5). | `likely, possible, unlikely, very-unlikely` |
| A target of 18, lower is better, projected 19 (range 18–20): d = (18 − 19) × −1 / 1 = 1. | `possible` |
| The 30→75 goal with 36, 39, 42, 45 in weeks 1–4, seen in week 4. | `plan: 1 pt ahead of plan [good] (plan 44%); since: 3 pts better [good] (was 42% in week 3); target: 30 pts to go [flat] (target 75%); hit: Very unlikely [bad] (likely 72% by cycle end)` |
| Short or over: higher is better, then lower is better. | `short, over` |
| A 60→30 goal (lower is better) with 50, 48, 46, 45 in weeks 1–4, seen in week 4: To target. | `15 pts over [flat] (target 30%)` |
| The same, but stale. | `hit: Can’t say` |

## Not self-explanatory

- **Not self-explanatory:** The scorecard’s words (labels, values and sub lines, including how units are said: “%” differences as pts, a unit made singular at 1, numbers padded to the goal’s decimals) are not all written out here. The conformance data gives every cell for every goal and week; a rebuild that matches each cell’s key, tone and likelihood has the rule, and the words follow `src/domain/scorecard.ts` and `src/domain/format.ts`.

## Requirements

- `GOAL-PAGE-SCORECARD`: Under a goal's status and number, a scorecard of labelled cells (two by two on a phone, in a row on a wider screen), each a value and one muted line: for a number goal vs plan, vs last week (the latest check-in against the one before, naming the week compared, worse or better by which way is good, with a drawn arrow), to target, and will it hit the target (Likely, Possible, Unlikely or Very unlikely, from where the target sits against the projected range, never a percentage); for a range vs the limit, vs last week, room to the limit and will it stay within; for dated stages stages done, stages late and when the next stage lands. The target is said once in the first screen; the chart marks the same numbers where they are (the gap to plan at now, the likely end, and what's left to the target) and nothing under it restates them, beyond one footnote on where the likely end comes from. Every section below the chart has a heading, one line on what it answers and a full-width rule above it; the owner's reason opens Why, and how the goals feeding it stand opens What feeds it.
- `PROJECTION-RANGE`: The projection is steady on a noisy number and called exactly on a clean trend: one more noisy week moves it by a few points, not tens; it is a range everywhere it's shown (the chart, Home and reviews' warnings, exports and the AI assistant's get_goal).
- `HONEST-NUMBERS`: Numbers people can trust. A whole workbook loads back for a goal owner, with only the rows they changed checked against who may change them. Every earlier plan is kept with the week it stopped applying, so old weeks and closed quarters stay judged against the plan of their day. A goal that measures a share can't report over 100%, and a value has to be a number before any status is shown. A goal gone quiet has no forecast in any view or export. A table compares a number with the plan for the same week. Exports judge every past check-in against the plan of its own week, as the screens do. What the map shows, the count, the link and "what's shown now" in Export are the same goals; goals drawn only for context are greyed and say so. While goals still have no check-in, the app says how many have reported rather than showing nothing needs attention; a milestone with no check-in isn't called on schedule, and the critical path only runs through goals whose status is known.

## Tests that check it

### [src/domain/scorecard.test.ts](../../../src/domain/scorecard.test.ts)

- will it hit the target: where the target sits against the projected range › likely when the target sits comfortably on the near side of the likeliest value, or below the whole range
- will it hit the target: where the target sits against the projected range › possible when the target is close to the likeliest value or inside the range on its better side
- will it hit the target: where the target sits against the projected range › unlikely when the target is beyond the range by up to half its width; very unlikely further
- will it hit the target: where the target sits against the projected range › reads the same way round when lower is better
- will it hit the target: where the target sits against the projected range › a clean trend with no spread still has a little doubt, from the floor
- amounts say their unit once, in the singular for one › hours, days and points
- the scorecard on made-up goals › a number goal, lower is better: vs plan, vs last week, to target, and will it hit
- the scorecard on made-up goals › a skipped week: the sub-line names the week compared
- the scorecard on made-up goals › a goal gone quiet says nothing about where it lands
- the scorecard on made-up goals › a stopped goal says how it stood and makes no forecast: no “will it hit?”, no likely end on the chart
- the scorecard on made-up goals › a range: vs the limit, vs last week, room to the limit, and will it stay within
- the scorecard on the example › lead time for changes: behind plan and very unlikely to reach 24 hours
- the scorecard on the example › dated stages: done, late, and the next one due
- the scorecard on the example › every goal gets a card that never says a percentage chance
